 Judgment
[LA.App. Nos.638/2012, 608/2012, 634/2012, 639/2012]
1.

These appeals arise from four land acquisition references, which are disposed of by the Reference
Court by a common judgment.
The Requisitioning
Authority has filed these appeals.
The land was acquired as per Section 4(1) Notification dated 17.09.2007.
The Land Acquisition Officer categorized the land into three categories.
The first category is shown as property having road frontage and the land value is fixed at Rs. 3,863/- per Are.
The second category is the land that does not have road frontage, lying just behind category No.1, in which the land value is fixed at Rs.3,708/- per Are.
The 3rd category is the land which lies behind 2025:KER:51111 LA.APP. NOS. 638, 608, 634 & 639 OF 2012 category No.2, in which the land value is fixed at Rs.3,553/- per Are.
2. The Reference Court interfered with the categorization and made two categories by clubbing category Nos.2 and 3 together.
The Reference Court granted compensation, fixing land value at the rate of Rs. 81,000 per Are for category No.1 and Rs. 71,000/- per Are for category Nos.2 and 3.
The Requisitioning Authority is challenging the enhancement of land value given by the Reference Court.
3. I heard the learned counsel for the appellant, Sri.Vishnu, the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants, Sri. Rinny Stephen and the learned Senior Government Pleader, Smt. Rekha C. Nair.

4. The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that the Reference Court ought to have made deductions 2025:KER:51111 LA.APP. NOS. 638, 608, 634 & 639 OF 2012 from Ext.A2 document when relying on the said document to fix the land value.

It is clear from the evidence that The Managing Director vs Gopala Pillai (Deceased) on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/194673014/
8 the Ext.A2 document is with respect to reclaimed land, whereas the acquired land is wetland.
The Reference Court ought to have taken the average of Exts.A2 and A4 documents, which were proximate to the date of acquisition.
The learned counsel for the appellant further contended that the Reference Court ought not to have interfered with the categorization.
The learned Senior Government Pleader also supported the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant.

5. On the other hand, the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants contended that the Reference Court correctly relied on Ext.A2 document, which is the document having the highest value among Exts. A2 to A4 documents 2025:KER:51111 LA.APP. NOS. 638, 608, 634 & 639 OF 2012 before it.
The Commission Report would reveal that Ext.A2 property is situated about 850 meters away from the acquired land lying on the side of the very same road.
6. I have considered the rival contentions.
7. Regarding the categorization, I find that the Reference Court categorized the properties into two categories- one category having road frontage and the other category having no road frontage.
Both category Nos.2 and 3 categorized by the Land Acquisition Officer are situated behind category No.1.
The extent involved is small.
In such a situation, the properties having no road frontage are to be treated as one category having the same value.

Hence, the Reference Court rightly treated category Nos.2 and 3 property as the same category No.2.
2025:KER:51111 LA.APP. NOS. 638, 608, 634 & 639 OF 2012 8.

Even though the Reference Court has not detailed as to how the land value is fixed, it appears that the Reference Court relied on Ext.A2 document, in which the land value is Rs.62,009 per Are and by giving an addition of 15% per annum for two years for the time difference and fixed the land value for category No.1 at Rs.81,000/-.
9.
The contention of the learned counsel for the appellant is that Ext.A2 property is reclaimed land.
The Section 4(1) notification is dated 17.09.2007, as on that date, the Kerala Conservation of Paddy and Wetland Act, prohibiting reclamation of wetland, was not in force.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Both Ext.A2 property and the acquired property were having road frontage.
Going by the Commission Report, the acquired property is reclaimed land.

As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the appellant, the Reference Court ought 2025:KER:51111 LA.APP. NOS. 638, 608, 634 & 639 OF 2012 to have taken the average value of Ext.A2 and A4 documents, as the Ext.A3 document is of the year 2001 and the same is liable to be excluded from calculation.
In Ext.A2, the land value is Rs.62,009/- per Are.
In Ext.A4, the land value is Rs.56,250/- per Are.
30% addition is to be given for the time difference of two years between Exts.A2 & A4 and Section 4(1) Notification.
After giving such addition, if the average value of Exts.A2 and A4 documents are taken, the average value would come around to Rs.76,868/- per Are.
Considering the fact that the acquired land is recorded as wetland, I am of the view that the value for category No.1 can be fixed at Rs.75,000/- per Are.
The difference between the land value fixed by the Reference Court with respect to category No.1 and 2 is Rs.10,000/- per Are.

I am of the view that the land value for category Nos.2 and 3 can be fixed at 2025:KER:51111 LA.APP.

Accordingly, L.A.A. No. 634/2012 is allowed in part, fixing the land value at Rs.75,000/- per Are for the acquired land.
L.A.A. Nos. 608/2012, 638/2012 and 639/2012 are allowed, fixing the land value at Rs.66,000/- per Are for the acquired land.
The claimants are entitled to get all statutory benefits and interest for the same.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The land was acquired as per Section 4(1) Notification dated 17.09.2007.
The Land Acquisition Officer categorized the land into three categories.
2. The Reference Court interfered with the categorization and made two categories by clubbing category Nos.2 and 3 together.
The Reference Court granted compensation, fixing land value at the rate of Rs. 81,000 per Are for category No.1 and Rs. 71,000/- per Are for category Nos.2 and 3.
The Requisitioning Authority is challenging the enhancement of land value given by the Reference Court.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The Reference Court ought to have taken the average of Exts.A2 and A4 documents, which were proximate to the date of acquisition.
The learned counsel for the appellant further contended that the Reference Court ought not to have interfered with the categorization.
The Section 4(1) notification is dated 17.09.2007, as on that date, the Kerala Conservation of Paddy and Wetland Act, prohibiting reclamation of wetland, was not in force.
Both Ext.A2 property and the acquired property were having road frontage.
Going by the Commission Report, the acquired property is reclaimed land.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Both category Nos.2 and 3 categorized by the Land Acquisition Officer are situated behind category No.1.
In such a situation, the properties having no road frontage are to be treated as one category having the same value.
opennyai_summary.decision:
In Ext.A2, the land value is Rs.62,009/- per Are.
In Ext.A4, the land value is Rs.56,250/- per Are.
30% addition is to be given for the time difference of two years between Exts.A2 & A4 and Section 4(1) Notification.
After giving such addition, if the average value of Exts.A2 and A4 documents are taken, the average value would come around to Rs.76,868/- per Are.
Considering the fact that the acquired land is recorded as wetland, I am of the view that the value for category No.1 can be fixed at Rs.75,000/- per Are.
The difference between the land value fixed by the Reference Court with respect to category No.1 and 2 is Rs.10,000/- per Are.
I am of the view that the land value for category Nos.2 and 3 can be fixed at 2025:KER:51111 LA.APP.
